feedback: REJECT — the candidate encodes the wrong specification: it is the mission chain (key -> door -> box), while the task is the response rule Response(blocker_moved, has_door_key): 'whenever the ball is out of the way, hold the key then or pick it up afterwards'. Decisive faults: (1) FINAL_STATES u3 is declared but not accepting for the task: reaching u3 requires target_picked_up, an event the task never mentions. A fully compliant agent that picks up the key while the ball is away and simply keeps holding it (or re-picks it after every loss) satisfies the task but never leaves u1/u2, so the RM withholds acceptance from task-satisfying behavior. (2) Missing regression: the domain defines key_lost as a one-step event ('true for that one step, not until the key is picked up again') precisely so the RM can re-arm the obligation when the key is dropped while the door is closed; the candidate never references key_lost (it is swallowed by the else self-loops), so the pending/discharged distinction collapses and the post-key_lost re-pickup earns no discharge reward, breaking progress density across the trigger->discharge->re-trigger cycle. (3) Task-irrelevant rewarded transitions: door_open (+0.2) and target_picked_up (+1.0) are not part of the response rule; attaching the largest reward to a non-task condition misaligns the shaping. (4) Ordered transition coverage for the rule (initial obligation, since blocker_moved is true and hands are empty at step 1; discharge on has_door_key; regression on key_lost; discharge again) is not represented — the only defensible hop is u0->(blocker_moved & has_door_key)->u1, which is in effect the discharge transition, but everything after it belongs to a different task. Minor notes: the u0 guard's blocker_moved conjunct slightly over-constrains discharge in the corner case where the agent re-blocks the front cell before its first key pickup (has_door_key alone discharges an obligation created while the ball was away); on the positive side the format matches the paper template (nonempty declared FINAL_STATES, predicate-only guards, per-state else self-loops, all four states reachable, bounded non-negative rewards), and the gating accidentally forces re-pickup after a closed-door drop because the door cannot be opened keyless — but gating is not acceptance, and the structure remains the mission RM. Expected shape (direction only, not a rewrite): a compact obligation automaton of ~2-3 states — initial/pending state left by the discharge (blocker_moved & has_door_key) into the accepting state, an explicit regression (key_lost) from the accepting state back to pending, no door_open or target_picked_up transitions, with the discharge (and each re-discharge) carrying the bounded progress/final reward. As submitted, semantic fidelity, final-state acceptance, regression explicitness, and transition-coverage criteria all fail, so the candidate cannot be accepted.

candidate:
REWARD_MACHINE:
STATES: u0, u1
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u1
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, key_lost) -> u0
(u1, else) -> u1
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, has_door_key, u1) -> 1.0
(u1, key_lost, u0) -> -1.0
feedback: Well-formed and faithful to the task. Format: exact paper layout with a nonempty FINAL_STATES header (u1), u1 declared in STATES and accepting, INITIAL_STATE declared, and every reward row paired with an existing transition. Reachability/compactness: u1 is reachable from u0 via has_door_key (the key is acquirable without touching the ball), and 2 states is minimal for 'key acquired and not since lost with the door closed'. Predicate-only labels: edges use only given propositions plus per-state else self-loops, so blocker_moved, door_open, target_picked_up and no-change steps are absorbed with no dead ends. Omitting blocker_moved from the labels is sound for this level: blocker_moved is guaranteed true at the first step, so the response obligation is active from the start and triggering directly on has_door_key is behaviorally equivalent (the else loops cover later blocker changes). Persistent/event distinction is correct: key_lost is a one-step event edge out of u1 (it can only follow a has_door_key step, so it always fires while in u1), while persistent has_door_key is awarded once per achievement because the machine leaves u0 and the u1 else-loop does not re-fire it. Regressions are explicit where the task requires them: a closed-door drop fires key_lost, u1->u0 with -1, and re-pickup is required and re-rewarded (+1) to return to the accepting state; crucially, the door-open drop does NOT regress because key_lost requires door_open false, matching the level's note that the canonical solve (pickup, toggle, open-door drop, box pickup) ends in u1. Rewards are dense progress signals, bounded at +/-1, with no reward on irrelevant transitions and no unbounded accumulation for a single achievement. Minor note (non-blocking): the only theoretical divergence is an adversarial corner where the agent re-blocks the door before a closed-door key drop and never re-picks; the level's own semantics key the regression to the key_lost event, which this RM encodes exactly.

feedback: All five declared propositions are implemented and no extra functions are present. blocker_moved: derives the cell in front of the door from the unique door's position (checks the cell at x-1 for each door), equivalent to the specified (dx-1, dy) cell; the x > 0 guard keeps grid.get in bounds, ball-in-hand counts as moved (not on the grid), it is a current-state condition so it goes false if the ball is dropped back, and it is true at the first step since the ball starts away. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the specified expressions exactly (carrying check, door scan with color match, is_open check, mission f-string match). key_lost correctly implements event semantics: previous_valuation['has_door_key'] true, has_door_key false now, door_open false now, false otherwise; it reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] without mutating it and gracefully returns False if the snapshot is absent. No imports, no actions, no side effects, only documented API access (env.grid.get, env.carrying, env.mission, env.width, env.height, episode_memory), empty cells guarded before attribute reads, and the code is syntactically valid Python.
